# ModConfig <Badge type="info" text="class" />

<p class="api-meta">Namespace <code>Lustral</code> · Assembly <code>Lustral.Api</code></p>

A mod's settings file, `Lustral/config/<id>.toml` in the game folder. Users edit the file, and the mod reads it into a settings class.

```csharp
public sealed class Settings
{
    [Description("Show the frame rate in the corner.")]
    public bool ShowFps { get; set; }
    public float Volume { get; set; } = 0.8f;
}

var settings = Config.Bind<Settings>();   // in the mod class
```

The file is stored outside the mod's folder, so settings are preserved when the mod is updated or reinstalled.

```csharp
public abstract class ModConfig
```

## Methods

### Bind&lt;T&gt;() {#bind}

```csharp
public abstract T Bind<T>() where T : class, new();
```

Reads the settings file into a new instance of `T`.

**Remarks**

Each public property with a getter and a setter is a setting. Its key in the file is the property name in snake\_case (`ShowFps` becomes `show_fps`), and its initial value is the default. Supported types are `bool`, `string`, integer and floating-point types, enumerations (stored by name), arrays and lists of these types, and nested classes, which are stored as TOML tables. A `[Description]` attribute (System.ComponentModel) is written as a comment above the setting.

Missing settings keep their defaults, and the file is rewritten with all settings so that users can see them; comments added by users are not preserved. Invalid values and unknown settings are logged and ignored. If the file is not valid TOML, it is left unchanged and all settings keep their defaults.

### Save&lt;T&gt;(T) {#save}

```csharp
public abstract void Save<T>(T settings) where T : class;
```

Writes `settings` to the settings file, for example after the user changes them in game.
